newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NAB plans A$1.1 bln share buy back.
newsitem.headline: NAB plans A$1.1 bln share buy back.

text.p: The National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB) said on Friday it planned to buy back on market up to 74 million shares at a cost of about A$1.1 billion at current market prices.
It also said it was working with an international investment bank to finalise a new flexible capital instrument that would raise up to US$750 million.

The bank said it was working with a major international investment bank to finalise a capital instrument that was in the form of tier two capital on issue and exchangeable at the National's option into tier one capital.

Both of the initiatives and the recently announced buy-back of an estimated 13 million shares would be subject to satisfactory market conditions and were expected to be completed over the next 12 months, it said.

NAB managing director Don Argus said all of the initiatives were designed to obtain the maximum value from the group's capital base. "In an increasingly complex and dynamic business environment we need to manage our capital to ensure we meet flexibility and cost objectives," Argus said.
"Higher levels of Tier One capital provide strategic flexibility, particularly in taking advantage of acquisition opportunities," he said.
"This needs to be balanced by consideration of the cost in financial performance terms of maintaining that higher capital base," Argus said.
He said documentation, legal and registration requirements needed to be completed before full details can be released.
The structure for the issue would need shareholder approvals at NAB's annual meeting in January.
"The instrument is expected to raise up to US$750 million," NAB said.
"It will be a US dollar denominated capital instrument offered to an overseas investor base."
"Apart from the capital raising aspect, the National believes this approach will have the added advantage of increasing international equity interest in the company's shares."
The instrument would be convertible at any time at the investor's option into ordinary shares at a conversion premium, NAB said.
NAB's shares closed up eight cents at A$14.84 on Thursday.
